hook.line: No gatekeeping. This is gonna annoy a lot of developers, but I want to share it.
hook.visual: He swings into frame in an orange hoodie at a podcast mic on a purple wall; label 'End of Front-End devs?' and yellow-highlighted word captions on top.

beats.what: Lunges into frame; persistent 'End of Front-End devs?' label and 'Gatekeeping.' caption
Teases controversy: this will annoy developers
Cut to a UI/UX landing-page image on a neon-light background: 'convert this image to code?'
Split screen: him on the left, tool screen recording on the right; drags the screenshot in
Picks the output language from a dropdown (React, Vue, Svelte...)
Result: the rebuilt landing page and its code appear side by side
Floating code window over neon lines as he says copy or download
CTA: comment a word to get the tool's name

why_it_works: Physical entrance (he lunges into frame at 0 s) plus 'no gatekeeping' creates motion and a secret in the first second
Fear-based label 'End of Front-End devs?' stays on screen as a standing question that the demo answers
Input image shown first, then the generated page: a clear before/after in under 20 s
Comment-a-word-for-the-name CTA withholds the tool name, which explains 3,052 comments
weaknesses: Tool name is deliberately hidden, which frustrates viewers and buries the value in the comments
Code and UI text in the split-screen recording are tiny on a phone
for_robert: Copy the entrance: start with Fred physically swimming or crashing into frame at 0 s instead of a static first frame, and keep a short provocative question label pinned on screen while the demo answers it.
